issues.summary: [PROJECT-GUIDE] Agent execution contract, readiness gate and delivery order
issues.outcome: A versioned Jira catalog prevents generic or incomplete tickets from being dispatched and synchronizes managed Jira fields without rewriting completed history or workflow state.
issues.context: The v1.2 catalog covered every issue but generated broad acceptance text and synthetic permissions. Catalog v1.3 makes semantic readiness enforceable, shards specifications by epic, and adds canary-only synchronization plus an explicit promotion gate.
inScope: Compile all v1.3 epic shards into one deterministic 401-record catalog and reject duplicate Source-IDs or Jira keys.
Reject executable leaves that lack concrete repository paths, artifacts, authorization actions, AC-to-test mapping, reproducible commands, or refined parents.
Synchronize descriptions, labels, Module, parents, issue types, and typed dependency links with backup, optimistic concurrency, canary limits, and no implicit creation or workflow transition.
outOfScope: Unlisted provider credentials and production policy values.
Direct cross-service database reads or duplicated ownership.
Unreviewed workflow transitions, historical rewrites, or destructive migration shortcuts.
businessRules: A decision is publishable only after named owner approval, effective time, supersession rule, fixtures, and rollback impact are recorded.
Example values are DRAFT/UAT only unless an explicit production policy is maker-checker approved.

contracts.name: Atlassian Jira Cloud REST API v3
contracts.compatibility: Use Source-ID and Jira key identity, preserve comments, worklogs, attachments, sprint and status, and abort on concurrent updated timestamps.

contracts.name: ViStay Jira catalog v1.3 JSON schema
contracts.compatibility: v1.2 stays immutable; v1.3 is compiled from per-epic shards and validated before synchronization.

interfaces: Version GraphQL/gRPC/Kafka/OpenAPI contracts before consumer implementation; document owner, caller, schema version, timeout, and compatibility.
Callable HTTP/GraphQL workflows include success, authorization-negative, validation, conflict, replay, and dependency-failure Postman examples.
Events use transactional outbox/inbox, stable aggregate identity, event ID, occurred-at time, producer schema version, and replay-safe consumers.
dataOwnership: Versioned policy and decision records are owned by platform_contracts; runtime services consume published versions and never silently invent defaults.
stateMachine: Specification moves from needs-refinement or decision-required to executable only after semantic validation; executable leaves become agent-ready or agent-ready-after-dependencies from live dependency state.
Jira workflow transitions are never performed by catalog synchronization; Ready promotion and Backlog demotion use the separate promotion gate.
Completed Jira issues are historical and their descriptions remain immutable; remediation is represented by a new Bug or Tech Debt issue.

dataPartitions: PROJECT:SCRUM only; credentials must have explicit project permission and may not enumerate other Jira projects.
fieldGroups: DELIVERY_SPEC is managed from the catalog; WORKFLOW_EVIDENCE, COMMENTS, ATTACHMENTS, WORKLOGS, SPRINT and STATUS remain Jira-owned.

failureSemantics: Return stable validation, forbidden, not-found, conflict, stale-revision, dependency-unavailable, and rate-limit codes without leaking PII.
Fail closed when authorization, authoritative projection, policy version, or required dependency is unavailable.
Retry only transient operations with bounded exponential backoff; route exhausted asynchronous work to a visible repair queue.
idempotencyConcurrency: Every externally retried mutation requires a scoped idempotency key, canonical request fingerprint, durable result, and mismatch rejection.
Use expected revision or equivalent compare-and-swap; concurrent winners are deterministic and losers receive conflict with current revision.
Consumers deduplicate by event ID and business key and support replay without duplicating money, inventory, notification, or audit effects.

acceptanceCriteria.given: the 26 v1.3 source shards containing all managed project issues
acceptanceCriteria.when: npm run validate:jira is executed in platform_contracts
acceptanceCriteria.then: one deterministic 401-record catalog is built, all Jira keys are present, and structural plus semantic validation succeeds

acceptanceCriteria.given: an open issue still contains generator boilerplate or lacks a concrete path, artifact, authorization action, AC mapping, or command
acceptanceCriteria.when: that issue is marked executable or dispatchable
acceptanceCriteria.then: validation fails and the issue cannot receive agent-ready

acceptanceCriteria.given: a reviewed catalog and a fresh Jira backup
acceptanceCriteria.when: a canary Apply is requested for at most five Source-IDs
acceptanceCriteria.then: only those issues are updated, any concurrent Jira edit aborts the run, no workflow status changes, and a repeated selected DryRun reports zero changes

tests: Catalog build and semantic validation cover identity, hierarchy, readiness, repository, authorization, acceptance, test-command, and evidence invariants.
Jira Validate and DryRun cover credential access, catalog-to-live identity, Module options, typed links, managed-field drift, backup, and reviewable plan generation.
Canary Apply plus selected zero-diff DryRun proves idempotent synchronization without touching Jira-owned workflow evidence.

testCases.evidence: platform_contracts console output showing 401 valid records, readiness counts, zero unsafe dispatchable records, and zero missing Jira keys
timestamped Jira backup and JSON dry-run plan for SCRUM-537
Apply result followed by a selected DryRun with changes=0 and unchanged Jira workflow status

observability: Propagate trace and correlation IDs across GraphQL/gRPC/Kafka/webhook boundaries without logging secrets or protected fields.
Emit transition, latency, error-code, replay/deduplication, dependency, and repair-queue metrics with bounded-cardinality labels.
Provide dashboard/alert thresholds and a runbook for stuck states, reconciliation mismatch, and rollback.
definitionOfDone: Catalog validation and all affected repository CI checks pass.
Contracts, migrations, compatibility path, implementation, Admin Web/Mobile parity where applicable, and Postman/Newman evidence are merged.
Security-negative, concurrency/replay, observability, reconciliation, and rollback evidence is linked in Jira.
No production secret or unapproved monetary/policy default is committed; ServiceOwner acceptance evidence is attached before Done.
evidence: Pull request and commit links per repository.
Automated test and Newman report with fixture version.
Migration/rollback or compatibility evidence where data/contracts change.
Dashboard, trace, audit, and reconciliation screenshots or machine-readable artifacts.
issues.decisionNoteVi: Các quy tắc nghiệp vụ và ranh giới dữ liệu trong catalog v1.2 đã được chốt; thay đổi sau này phải tạo phiên bản policy/contract mới, không sửa ngược lịch sử.

issues.context: This epic is part of the ViStay VS-E01 delivery boundary. The specification is canonical for implementation detail; Jira remains canonical for workflow and delivery evidence.
inScope: Implement and verify: Platform Baseline & Executable Walking Skeleton.
Version contract, persistence, authorization, failure, audit, and operator behavior needed by this outcome.
Provide repository-specific automated tests and Postman/Newman evidence for callable APIs.
outOfScope: Unlisted provider credentials and production policy values.
Direct cross-service database reads or duplicated ownership.
Unreviewed workflow transitions, historical rewrites, or destructive migration shortcuts.
businessRules: The walking slice must traverse Nginx, Hive Router, service authorization, database, Kafka, and SSE with trace propagation.
Configuration and secrets fail closed; example files contain no live credentials.
interfaces: Version GraphQL/gRPC/Kafka/OpenAPI contracts before consumer implementation; document owner, caller, schema version, timeout, and compatibility.
Callable HTTP/GraphQL workflows include success, authorization-negative, validation, conflict, replay, and dependency-failure Postman examples.
Events use transactional outbox/inbox, stable aggregate identity, event ID, occurred-at time, producer schema version, and replay-safe consumers.
dataOwnership: Each service owns its database; Keycloak owns credentials/sessions; authorization DB is source of truth and Redis is cache only.
stateMachine: Model legal states and transitions for Platform Baseline & Executable Walking Skeleton; reject illegal transitions with stable error codes.
Persist actor, reason, source, policy/contract version, expected revision, and timestamps for every material transition.
Terminal or superseded records are retained; corrections use a new revision or compensating record.

dataPartitions: SYSTEM for internal repair only; otherwise enforce the subject account type and the resource customer, host-party, site, branch, or assigned-employee partition.
fieldGroups: SUMMARY by default; FINANCIAL, PII, DOCUMENT, TRUST_DETAIL, and INTERNAL_AUDIT require explicit grants and response-field filtering.

failureSemantics: Return stable validation, forbidden, not-found, conflict, stale-revision, dependency-unavailable, and rate-limit codes without leaking PII.
Fail closed when authorization, authoritative projection, policy version, or required dependency is unavailable.
Retry only transient operations with bounded exponential backoff; route exhausted asynchronous work to a visible repair queue.
idempotencyConcurrency: Every externally retried mutation requires a scoped idempotency key, canonical request fingerprint, durable result, and mismatch rejection.
Use expected revision or equivalent compare-and-swap; concurrent winners are deterministic and losers receive conflict with current revision.
Consumers deduplicate by event ID and business key and support replay without duplicating money, inventory, notification, or audit effects.

acceptanceCriteria.given: an authorized actor with a valid partition and a complete request for Platform Baseline & Executable Walking Skeleton
acceptanceCriteria.when: the command or query is executed
acceptanceCriteria.then: the documented outcome, state revision, audit record, and contract response are produced deterministically

acceptanceCriteria.given: a caller missing the action, partition, or requested field-group grant
acceptanceCriteria.then: access is denied without leaking existence or restricted fields and the denial is auditable

acceptanceCriteria.given: the same mutation is replayed or two requests use the same expected revision
acceptanceCriteria.then: at most one business effect is committed and all responses are stable, explainable, and reconciled

tests: Unit tests cover rule boundaries, legal/illegal transitions, rounding/timezone where relevant, and stable error mapping.
Integration tests cover persistence constraints, authorization action+partition+field groups, outbox/inbox replay, and dependency failure.
Postman/Newman flow covers happy path, negative authorization, validation, conflict, idempotent replay, and a cleanup-safe deterministic fixture.
observability: Propagate trace and correlation IDs across GraphQL/gRPC/Kafka/webhook boundaries without logging secrets or protected fields.
Emit transition, latency, error-code, replay/deduplication, dependency, and repair-queue metrics with bounded-cardinality labels.
Provide dashboard/alert thresholds and a runbook for stuck states, reconciliation mismatch, and rollback.
definitionOfDone: Catalog validation and all affected repository CI checks pass.
Contracts, migrations, compatibility path, implementation, Admin Web/Mobile parity where applicable, and Postman/Newman evidence are merged.
Security-negative, concurrency/replay, observability, reconciliation, and rollback evidence is linked in Jira.
No production secret or unapproved monetary/policy default is committed; ServiceOwner acceptance evidence is attached before Done.
evidence: Pull request and commit links per repository.
Automated test and Newman report with fixture version.
Migration/rollback or compatibility evidence where data/contracts change.
Dashboard, trace, audit, and reconciliation screenshots or machine-readable artifacts.
issues.decisionNoteVi: Các quy tắc nghiệp vụ và ranh giới dữ liệu trong catalog v1.2 đã được chốt; thay đổi sau này phải tạo phiên bản policy/contract mới, không sửa ngược lịch sử.

issues.summary: [VS-E03-S01-ST01] Implement authorized presigned upload sessions
issues.actor: Authorized backoffice operator or trusted ViStay service
issues.outcome: Media Service creates a bounded upload session and returns private, short-lived presigned upload instructions only after action, partition, file-count, type, and size authorization succeeds.
issues.context: The baseline migration already contains upload_sessions and media_assets. Implement the missing domain/application/persistence/object-store adapters and GraphQL mutation without moving binary content into PostgreSQL.
inScope: Add authorizeMediaUpload GraphQL input/payload and stable error mapping.
Validate 1..20 files, per-file JPEG/PNG/WebP <=15 MiB or PDF <=25 MiB, total <=100 MiB, sanitized filenames, and session expiry.
Persist PENDING upload session/assets and generate private object keys and presigned PUT URLs with content-type and checksum constraints.
Write audit and outbox rows in the creation transaction.
outOfScope: Frontend rendering outside the owning service contract.
Direct reads from another service database.
Production credentials, destructive history rewrites, or silent fallback authorization.
businessRules: Allow JPEG/PNG/WebP up to 15 MiB and PDF up to 25 MiB; one session allows at most 20 files and 100 MiB.
Reject video, SVG, Office, and HEIC initially; verify magic bytes, malware status, checksum, and strip image EXIF.
Upload/download URLs are short lived and objects remain private.
interfaces: Expose only the operations named in this issue through the owning GraphQL or gRPC boundary.
Return stable validation, forbidden, not-found, conflict, and dependency-unavailable codes.
Persist an outbox event in the same transaction for every externally observable state change.
dataOwnership: Media owns upload sessions, object metadata, checksum, scan state, retention state, access audit, and domain references; object bytes stay in private object storage.
stateMachine: Upload session begins PENDING and may issue URLs only until expiresAt.
The first accepted object transfer advances the session to UPLOADING; authorization alone does not mark content uploaded.
Expired or cancelled sessions cannot issue another URL; retries with the same idempotency key return the original session.

dataPartitions: ADMIN organization plus SITE/BRANCH membership for the target property; SYSTEM is limited to authenticated internal repair or projection calls.
fieldGroups: SUMMARY is baseline; DOCUMENT and INTERNAL_AUDIT require explicit field-group grants.

failureSemantics: Reject malformed or unauthorized calls before mutating state and do not reveal whether a restricted aggregate exists.
Map stale expectedVersion to CONFLICT_STALE_REVISION and unavailable required dependencies to DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE.
Retry only object-store, scanner, or event-publication failures classified as transient; retain the failed job for bounded repair.
idempotencyConcurrency: Require an idempotency key for commands that can be retried externally and persist its request fingerprint and result.
Use aggregate version compare-and-swap so concurrent writers produce one winner and a stable conflict for losers.
Deduplicate consumed events by event ID and business key.

issues.summary: [VS-E05] Pricing & Rate Rules
issues.outcome: Pricing hardening is split into durable Booking behavior, versioned contract evidence, authorization invalidation, and separate Admin Web/Mobile workspaces.
issues.context: Completed historical pricing Stories remain immutable; only the open Task/Subtask leaves below are dispatchable.
inScope: Implement and verify: Pricing & Rate Rules.
Version contract, persistence, authorization, failure, audit, and operator behavior needed by this outcome.

outOfScope: Unlisted provider credentials and production policy values.
Direct cross-service database reads or duplicated ownership.
Unreviewed workflow transitions, historical rewrites, or destructive migration shortcuts.
businessRules: Stay products are SHORT 1-29 nights, MEDIUM 30-364 nights, and LONG 365 or more nights; boundaries are versioned configuration.
Only SHORT supports the five discount price levels.
No hourly booking is allowed; default check-in 14:00 and checkout 12:00 are configurable property-local policy.
Staff markup may be fixed or percentage within configured cap and is persisted separately from base rate and discounts.
interfaces: Version GraphQL/gRPC/Kafka/OpenAPI contracts before consumer implementation; document owner, caller, schema version, timeout, and compatibility.
Callable HTTP/GraphQL workflows include success, authorization-negative, validation, conflict, replay, and dependency-failure Postman examples.
Events use transactional outbox/inbox, stable aggregate identity, event ID, occurred-at time, producer schema version, and replay-safe consumers.
dataOwnership: Booking/Pricing owns base commercial rate, dated rules, publication versions, quote calculation, and frozen quote snapshots; Property owns no base price.
stateMachine: Model legal states and transitions for Pricing & Rate Rules; reject illegal transitions with stable error codes.
Persist actor, reason, source, policy/contract version, expected revision, and timestamps for every material transition.
Terminal or superseded records are retained; corrections use a new revision or compensating record.

dataPartitions: SYSTEM for internal repair only; otherwise enforce the subject account type and the resource customer, host-party, site, branch, or assigned-employee partition.
fieldGroups: SUMMARY by default; FINANCIAL, PII, DOCUMENT, TRUST_DETAIL, and INTERNAL_AUDIT require explicit grants and response-field filtering.

failureSemantics: Return stable validation, forbidden, not-found, conflict, stale-revision, dependency-unavailable, and rate-limit codes without leaking PII.
Fail closed when authorization, authoritative projection, policy version, or required dependency is unavailable.
Retry only transient operations with bounded exponential backoff; route exhausted asynchronous work to a visible repair queue.
idempotencyConcurrency: Every externally retried mutation requires a scoped idempotency key, canonical request fingerprint, durable result, and mismatch rejection.
Use expected revision or equivalent compare-and-swap; concurrent winners are deterministic and losers receive conflict with current revision.
Consumers deduplicate by event ID and business key and support replay without duplicating money, inventory, notification, or audit effects.

issues.actor: Authorized backoffice operator or trusted ViStay service
issues.outcome: Booking Service converts a ready request into an immutable quote and, only when explicitly requested, a time-bounded tentative inventory hold using existing pricing and inventory contracts.
issues.context: Quote creation must not silently block inventory. A hold is a separate authorized command with its own idempotency key, expected inventory revision, expiry, and visible release path.
inScope: Add createQuoteFromRequest using an explicit published pricing version and persist request/lead/attribution references without copying mutable profiles.
Add createHoldFromRequest that calls the existing inventory block path with TENTATIVE status, policy-bounded expiry, correlation/idempotency key, and expected inventory revision.
Add releaseRequestHold and expiration reconciliation; quote-only flow leaves inventory unchanged.
On booking conversion, copy explicit creator/owner/sale attribution into booking_attributions with effective evidence and mark the request CONVERTED atomically.
outOfScope: Frontend rendering outside the owning service contract.
Direct reads from another service database.
Production credentials, destructive history rewrites, or silent fallback authorization.

interfaces: Expose only the operations named in this issue through the owning GraphQL or gRPC boundary.
Return stable validation, forbidden, not-found, conflict, and dependency-unavailable codes.
Persist an outbox event in the same transaction for every externally observable state change.
dataOwnership: Booking owns pre-customer lead contact envelopes, inquiries, booking requests, attribution, follow-up, quote/hold references, and their lifecycle audit. User owns account/customer profile identity; Booking stores only its stable reference after linkage.
stateMachine: Quote is ACTIVE -> USED, EXPIRED, or CANCELLED and never implies a hold.
Explicit hold is TENTATIVE -> ACTIVE on confirmed booking or RELEASED/CANCELLED on release/expiry; it uses existing overlap constraints.
Request becomes CONVERTED only after booking plus attribution commit succeeds; failed quote/hold never advances it falsely.

Use aggregate version compare-and-swap so concurrent writers produce one winner and a stable conflict for losers.
Deduplicate consumed events by event ID and business key.

Default waiver eligibility requires composite at least 80, payment at least 70, cleanliness at least 65, verified email, at least three completed stays spanning 90 days, and no hard blocker.
There is no direct score edit; corrections and reversals append facts and replay the projection under the original or explicitly selected policy version.
Positive, minor, and medium facts decay after 24 months; major/no-show facts after 36 months; active blockers do not decay.
A disputed negative fact blocks automatic waiver while pending but is not a final point deduction.

failureSemantics: Return stable validation, forbidden, not-found, conflict, stale-revision, dependency-unavailable, and rate-limit codes without leaking PII.

businessRules: The trust subject is the responsible customer account, not the employee who creates the booking; an absent customer account is UNASSESSED and requires full deposit.
Dimensions are Payment 30%, Booking 25%, Property care/cleanliness 30%, and Conduct 15%; identity/history are eligibility gates and confidence, not score points.
Each dimension starts at 50 and is clamped 0-100; tiers are RESTRICTED 0-39, WATCH 40-59, RELIABLE 60-79, TRUSTED 80-100; insufficient evidence displays UNASSESSED.
Default waiver eligibility requires composite at least 80, payment at least 70, cleanliness at least 65, verified email, at least three completed stays spanning 90 days, and no hard blocker.
There is no direct score edit; corrections and reversals append facts and replay the projection under the original or explicitly selected policy version.
Positive, minor, and medium facts decay after 24 months; major/no-show facts after 36 months; active blockers do not decay.
A disputed negative fact blocks automatic waiver while pending but is not a final point deduction.
Policies are effective-dated, simulated, maker-checker published, and historical decisions remain frozen.
interfaces: Version GraphQL/gRPC/Kafka/OpenAPI contracts before consumer implementation; document owner, caller, schema version, timeout, and compatibility.

dataOwnership: Finance owns normalized trust facts, effective-dated scoring policies, trust profile/tier/confidence, deposit decision, and appeal ledger; Operations owns raw cleanliness evidence; User owns identity; Booking freezes the decision snapshot.
stateMachine: Model legal states and transitions for service_user delivery slice for Compute explainable trust profile tier and confidence; reject illegal transitions with stable error codes.
Persist actor, reason, source, policy/contract version, expected revision, and timestamps for every material transition.
Terminal or superseded records are retained; corrections use a new revision or compensating record.

dataPartitions: SYSTEM for internal repair only; otherwise enforce the subject account type and the resource customer, host-party, site, branch, or assigned-employee partition.
fieldGroups: SUMMARY by default; FINANCIAL, PII, DOCUMENT, TRUST_DETAIL, and INTERNAL_AUDIT require explicit grants and response-field filtering.

failureSemantics: Return stable validation, forbidden, not-found, conflict, stale-revision, dependency-unavailable, and rate-limit codes without leaking PII.
Fail closed when authorization, authoritative projection, policy version, or required dependency is unavailable.
Retry only transient operations with bounded exponential backoff; route exhausted asynchronous work to a visible repair queue.
idempotencyConcurrency: Every externally retried mutation requires a scoped idempotency key, canonical request fingerprint, durable result, and mismatch rejection.
Use expected revision or equivalent compare-and-swap; concurrent winners are deterministic and losers receive conflict with current revision.
Consumers deduplicate by event ID and business key and support replay without duplicating money, inventory, notification, or audit effects.

businessRules: The trust subject is the responsible customer account, not the employee who creates the booking; an absent customer account is UNASSESSED and requires full deposit.
Dimensions are Payment 30%, Booking 25%, Property care/cleanliness 30%, and Conduct 15%; identity/history are eligibility gates and confidence, not score points.
Each dimension starts at 50 and is clamped 0-100; tiers are RESTRICTED 0-39, WATCH 40-59, RELIABLE 60-79, TRUSTED 80-100; insufficient evidence displays UNASSESSED.
Default waiver eligibility requires composite at least 80, payment at least 70, cleanliness at least 65, verified email, at least three completed stays spanning 90 days, and no hard blocker.
There is no direct score edit; corrections and reversals append facts and replay the projection under the original or explicitly selected policy version.
Positive, minor, and medium facts decay after 24 months; major/no-show facts after 36 months; active blockers do not decay.
A disputed negative fact blocks automatic waiver while pending but is not a final point deduction.
Policies are effective-dated, simulated, maker-checker published, and historical decisions remain frozen.
